title: Display and position
summary: Choose how elements flow with display, and place one element on top of another with position.

quiz.q: What is true of a **block** element such as `div` or `p`?
options: It sits in a line with its neighbours
It starts on a new line and takes the full available width
quiz.explain: Block elements stack vertically and stretch across their container. Inline elements such as `span` or `a` flow within a line of text.

quiz.q: Why would you use `display: inline-block` on a button-like link?
options: It keeps the link in the line but lets width and height apply
It makes the link a block on its own line
quiz.explain: `inline-block` sits in the line like text but behaves like a box inside, so width and height work properly, like they do on a block.

quiz.q: Remove an element from the page completely, without leaving a gap.
quiz.explain: `display: none` takes the element out of the layout. (`visibility: hidden` hides it but keeps its space.)

quiz.q: To place a badge in the top right corner of a card, put these steps in order.
quiz.explain: The parent becomes the reference with `position: relative`. The child is then offset from the parent's corner with `absolute` plus `top` and `right`.

quiz.q: An absolutely positioned element is placed relative to...
options: its nearest ancestor that has a position other than static
quiz.explain: If no ancestor is positioned, it uses the initial containing block, which is roughly the first screenful of the page. Setting `position: relative` on the parent is the usual way to control this.

exercise.task:
Control flow and position. Work in `index.html`.

- `.badge` is a `span`. Make it `display: inline-block` with a `width` of 100px.
- `.menu-link` is an `a`. Make it `display: block`.
- `.hidden-note` must be removed from the layout (`display: none`).
- `.panel` gets `position: relative`. `.corner` inside it gets `position: absolute`, `top: 0` and `right: 0`.
hints: Five elements, each needing one or two declarations. Start with `display`.
The parent needs `position: relative` so the child's `top` and `right` are measured from the parent.

checks.name: .badge is 100px wide
checks.hint: Width only works on inline-block or block. Add width: 100px;.

checks.name: .corner is at the top and right
